''''' Probability Theory and Related Fields''''' is a [[peer review|peer-reviewed]] [[mathematics journal]] published by [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]]. Established in 1962,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Probability Theory and Related Fields {{!}} Volume 1, issue 1|url=https://link.springer.com/journal/440/volumes-and-issues/1-1|access-date=2022-01-04|website=SpringerLink|language=en}}</ref> it was originally named '''''Zeitschrift für Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und verwandte Gebiete''''', with the English replacing the German starting from volume 71 (1986).<ref>{{Cite journal|date=January 1986|title=Announcement|url=https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/BF00366268.pdf|journal=Probability Theory and Related Fields|volume=71|pages=A3 |doi=10.1007/BF00366268}}</ref> The journal publishes articles on [[probability]]. The journal is indexed by ''[[Mathematical Reviews]]'' and [[Zentralblatt MATH]]. Its 2019 [[Mathematical Citation Quotient|MCQ]] was 2.29, and its 2019 [[impact factor]] was 2.125.

The current [[editors-in-chief]] are [[Fabio Toninelli]] (Technical University of Vienna) and [[Bálint Tóth]] (University of Bristol and Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Probability Theory and Related Fields|url=https://www.springer.com/journal/440|access-date=2022-01-04|website=Springer|language=en}}</ref>

The journal [[CiteScore]] is 3.8 and its [[SCImago Journal Rank]] is 3.198, both from 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Scopus preview - Scopus - Probability Theory and Related Fields|url=https://www.scopus.com/sourceid/25829|access-date=2022-01-04|website=www.scopus.com}}</ref> It is currently ranked 11th in the field of Probability & Statistics with Applications according to [[Google Scholar]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Probability & Statistics with Applications - Google Scholar Metrics|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=top_venues&hl=en&vq=phy_probabilitystatistics|access-date=2022-01-04|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

*1961–1971: [[Leopold Schmetterer]] (Vienna)
*1971–1985: [[:de:Klaus Krickeberg|Klaus Krickeberg]] (Bielefeld)
*1985–1991: [[Hermann Rost]] (Heidelberg)
*1991–1994: [[Olav Kallenberg]] (Auburn AL)
*1994–2000: [[Erwin Bolthausen]] (Zurich)
*2000–2005: [[Geoffrey Grimmett]] (Cambridge)
*2005–2010: [[Jean-François Le Gall]] (Paris) and [[Jean Bertoin]] (Paris)
*2010–2015: [[Gérard Ben Arous]] (New York) and [[Amir Dembo]] (Stanford)
*2015–2020: [[Michel Ledoux]] (Toulouse) and [[Fabio Martinelli]] (Rome)
*2021–2024: [[Fabio Toninelli]] (Vienna) and [[Bálint Tóth]]  (Budapest and Bristol)
